page_title: AI Coding Cost & Token Usage Tracker for Claude Code, Cursor & Codex | CodeBurn

summary.name: CodeBurn
summary.one_liner: CodeBurn is a free, open-source, local-first tool that tracks token usage and cost across AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, broken down by model, project and task.
keywords: how much does claude code cost
use_cases: track how much Claude Code or Cursor spending each month
see which model and project consume the most tokens
find wasteful token usage in coding agent sessions
monitor remaining plan usage limits for AI coding tools
estimate cost per pull request or coding session
compare AI coding tool spend without uploading data
summary.what_it_does: CodeBurn reads the session files already on the local machine for AI coding tools and reports token usage and cost. Totals can be viewed from today to lifetime, and split by model, project, activity type, core tools, shell commands, skills, agents and MCP servers. It shows cache hit rate, turns and one-shot percentage per row. Desktop, menu bar, VS Code extension and terminal views present the same data, and the page describes a per-session and per-pull-request cost view derived from transcripts. A codeburn optimize command grades setup and flags waste such as duplicate reads, with fixes that can be applied and undone.
notable: Reads local session files only; no account or API keys, and the page says nothing is uploaded
Covers 42 AI coding tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot and Gemini
Native Swift macOS menu bar app plus desktop app, VS Code extension, CLI and GNOME top bar
Optimize command grades setup A to F and can apply fixes with undo
caveats: The desktop app has optional anonymous telemetry that the user opts into at first launch
Some live capacity and plan-usage features are shown for providers the user is signed in to, and the page does not detail their coverage beyond that
The page lists 'Itemized' tool names inconsistently with the '42 tools' claim, and mentions 18+ tools in a testimonial, so the exact supported count is as stated on the page only
